title: Waves & Radioactivity - Calculations
welcome_lead: Calculations on Waves & Radioactivity for GCSE Physics.
meta_desc: Practise v=f lambda and half-life calculations.
final_note: You worked through wave equation and half-life sums.

mcqs.q: Activity after 3 half-lives is original times:
What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.
A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: The water turns into wave material and changes state.
Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
